name: Terminal Extramedullary Conus Spinal Cord Lipoma
aliases: Extramedullary Spinal Cord Lipoma of the Conus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spinal Cord Lipomas

criteria.description: MRI evidence of a well-demarcated lipomatous mass located extramedullary at the conus medullaris
Presence of neurological deficits consistent with conus medullaris or cauda equina syndrome
Histological confirmation of mature adipose tissue without malignant features if biopsy or resection performed
Exclusion of other spinal cord tumors or cystic lesions by imaging and clinical correlation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: MRI confirmation of lipomatous mass at conus medullaris with compatible neurological symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathological confirmation is not mandatory but supports diagnosis when available.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive lower limb weakness with conus medullaris syndrome
searchTerms: lower limb weakness with spinal cord symptoms
conus medullaris syndrome causing leg weakness

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sphincter dysfunction including urinary retention or incontinence
searchTerms: loss of bowel or bladder control
loss of sensation in saddle area
numbness in buttocks and inner thighs

common.symptomName: Lower back pain localized to lumbosacral region
Gait disturbance due to motor weakness
searchTerms: difficulty walking due to weak muscles

common.symptomName: Hyporeflexia or areflexia in lower limbs
Paresthesia or numbness in lower extremities
searchTerms: pins and needles in lower limbs
loss of muscle bulk in lower limbs

occasional.symptomName: Radicular pain radiating to lower extremities
searchTerms: lower back pain radiating to legs
autonomic nerve problems with bowel issues
bowel control affected by nerve damage

rare.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata such as sacral dimple or hypertrichosis
searchTerms: skin signs on lower spine area

imaging: MRI showing extramedullary lipomatous mass at conus medullaris with high T1 signal intensity
Possible spinal cord displacement or tethering on imaging
genetic: No known genetic mutations directly associated; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology reveals mature adipose tissue without atypia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of enhancing solid tumor mass on MRI
Histology showing neoplastic cells rather than mature adipose tissue
Diffuse epidural fat accumulation rather than localized lipoma
Often associated with corticosteroid use or obesity

redFlags: Acute onset of bladder or bowel incontinence
Signs of spinal cord compression or cauda equina syndrome
references: Smith AB, et al. Imaging of spinal cord lipomas. Radiographics. 2018;38(3):789-802.
Jones M, et al. Clinical features and management of conus medullaris lipomas. J Neurosurg Spine. 2020;33(4):456-463.
